title: Midnight Gilt — Art Déco Black-Tie Gala
description: A ceremonial invitation slide built on deep ink-black with warm 18-karat gold ornament and bone-ivory didone type — distinguished from other dark-gold templates by its strict art-deco bilateral symmetry, hairline foil frame, and a vertical axis that never breaks.
philosophy: This template exists for moments that demand gravitas: galas, award ceremonies, and luxury events where the opening slide is itself part of the occasion. It embraces extreme formal restraint — one vertical axis, two tones, and no decorative element that isn't load-bearing to the ceremony. It refuses gradients, off-center compositions, sans-serif type, and anything that reads as digital, casual, or contemporary. The room it is designed for is candlelit; the speaker does not need many slides.
goodFor: Gala and black-tie event opening title screens
Luxury brand or heritage product reveal title cards
Charity evening program cover and section dividers
avoidFor: Multi-column data tables or dashboard layouts
Informal internal team or all-hands announcements
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like the printed cover of a black-tie ceremony program — weighty, still, and inevitable in its formality. A strict single vertical axis holds every element in bilateral symmetry; nothing tilts, offsets, or wanders from that spine. An art-deco geometric motif — stepped arch, chevron, or sunburst — crowns the title as structural ornament rather than decorative flourish, anchoring the composition from above. Avoid any hint of digital modernity, casual asymmetry, or visual busyness; the prevailing mood is candlelit hush, where restraint itself carries all the drama.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed dark field with a hairline foil rule inset ~4% from all four edges, forming a strict bilateral border frame that is itself part of the composition. A single vertical center axis governs every element top-to-bottom: a geometric art-deco header device, the large title text block, a thin horizontal rule divider, and a subtitle line — with the lower quarter left entirely empty as ceremonial breathing room. Hierarchy is conveyed through scale contrast alone within the centered vertical stack; no header band, no page number, no asymmetric offset. The hairline border frame and the center axis are the only two load-bearing structural elements on the slide.

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like an engraved ceremony card held under candlelight — weighty, hushed, and entirely intentional. Bilateral symmetry is absolute; a central ornamental deco medallion or chevron glyph acts as the hinge between a short ceremonial label above and the primary honoree name or announcement copy below. Rhythm is slow and vertical: generous space between stacked elements lets each line breathe as a distinct event. Avoid any diagonal motion, photographic texture, icon-grid layouts, or compositional energy that reads as contemporary, crowded, or informal.

examples.layoutNotes: Single absolute vertical axis; all content elements — label, ornamental rule, primary text block, attribution or sub-copy — stack centered on that axis with no horizontal offset at any level. Outer hairline foil frame sits 4% inset from all four edges, unbroken. A pair of thin gold rule lines flanks the primary content block as structural dividers, not decoration. Section or program number appears bottom-center inside the frame, isolated by generous vertical clearance.
